subject: Exhibit B — Minimum Guarantee & Pricing Floor: counterproposal and redline
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julia Ramos <julia@horizon-analytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exhibit B redlines (minimum guarantee / floors)

Hi Julia — thanks for sending the redlines and the usage history. We reviewed the changes with Sales and Legal and wanted to propose a pragmatic counter to get you the predictability Horizon needs while protecting our economics. Highlights below; attached is a brief summary and we'll follow up with a tracked redline if this looks directionally correct.

Key proposal (high level)
- Minimum guarantee (MG): 12-month commitment at a baseline equal to 60% of Horizon's trailing-12 usage (calendarized) for Year 1, with an optional annual reset tied to actual usage.
- Ramp credit: first 6 months, overage credits applied if usage is below the baseline to smooth the onboarding ramp.
- Pricing floor / cap: simplify language — floor defined by the MG (above) and cap defined as 150% of baseline for compute surcharge calculations; overages beyond cap billed at standard metered rates.
- Discounting: we can extend a 15% volume discount off published list for the committed baseline; anything beyond that must follow our overage pricing.

Trade-offs we need from Horizon:
- Agreement to a 12-month term for the committed baseline (we can adopt a quarterly billing schedule).
- Removal of the unlimited rollback clause — we prefer a structured adjustment window on anniversary.

Next steps: if you can confirm these bullets, I'll circulate a tracked Exhibit B redline for signature and route the change through procurement/legal for final approval. Rishi — please flag if the discount cadence or the % is above your approval.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pricing_exhibit_v3.pdf (PDF, 42KB)]

From: Julia Ramos <julia@horizon-analytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exhibit B redlines (minimum guarantee / floors)

Laura — appreciate the rapid response. A few points from our side:
- We understand the need for a baseline, but Horizon's usage is seasonal and can drop below 50% in Q1. A hard 12-month MG at 60% could expose us in the first year.
- The ramp credit is promising; can that be modeled as a full credit for months 1–2 and a 50% credit months 3–6? That helps us smooth headcount-driven variability.
- On discounts: procurement will ask for at least a 20% committed discount on the baseline if we guarantee the 12-month MG.

I've attached our marked Exhibit B (Horizon_redlines_ExhibitB_v2.docx) with commentary from finance and procurement. Also looping Marcus, our legal lead, for contract language.

Thanks,
Julia Ramos
Head of Cloud Platform | Horizon Analytics

Subject: Re: Fwd: Exhibit B redlines (Horizon) — pricing/discount asks

Laura — quick read and my recommended counter below. High level: we can accept the 6-month ramp structure and bump the discount but with strict limits and measurement windows.

Recommended counter (Legal + Finance):
- MG baseline: keep 12-month term with baseline = 60% of T12, but include an explicit quarterly adjustment mechanism on each contract anniversary to true-up baseline up or down based on actual trailing usage.
- Ramp credits: months 1–2 = 100% credit; months 3–6 = 50% credit. Credits only apply to invoices where usage < baseline and do not create refundable credits beyond year-end.
- Discount: approve up to 18% discount on committed baseline without VP approval; any request >= 19% requires VP Sales sign-off.
- Cap/floor language: simplify — define floor as MG baseline, cap as 150% of baseline for surcharge math. Add a force-majeure carve and a 90-day cure window for payment disputes.
- Termination/remedies: clarify that failure to meet payment obligations is a remedy trigger; do not agree to unlimited rollback or retroactive credits.

If Sales wants to meet the customer's 20% ask, Rishi — we'll need a quick VP approval and an offset (either shorter term guarantee or prepayment). I can draft tracked ExhibitB_Redline_v3_Laura.docx with the language above tonight.

—Monica
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Julia / Marcus — thanks for the constructive feedback. Attached is our tracked Exhibit B (ExhibitB_Redline_v3_Laura.docx) implementing the ramp credit structure you proposed and the legal guardrails Monica outlined. Short summary of edits:
- Ramp credit: months 1–2 = 100% credit; months 3–6 = 50% credit applied when monthly usage < baseline.
- Baseline: Year 1 baseline = 60% of T12 (calendarized); annual adjustment window on anniversary to true-up.
- Discount: committed baseline receives 18% off published list; additional discount to 20% requires VP Sales approval.
- Cap/floor: floor = baseline; cap = 150% of baseline; over-cap usage billed at metered rates.
- Added 90-day cure for payment disputes and removed rollback language.

If the 18% vs 20% is the only blocker, Rishi and I can escalate to VP for discretionary approval with a proposed offset (either 6-month prepay or 10% increase in baseline for Year 2).

Please review the attached and let me know if we should proceed to DocuSign.

Best,
Laura Bennett
